subject.title: Feature: Add per-model generation timeout config

question: Should OpenClaw add a new public per-agent/per-model non-resetting generation timeout config, or keep operators on existing provider/run/idle/first-event timeout surfaces plus narrower thinking/repetition fixes?
rationale: The code path is identifiable, but the fix adds public config and changes fallback/abort semantics across providers, so automation should not choose the product contract.

options.title: Add generation timeout contract
options.body: Add a documented per-agent/per-model non-resetting generation timeout with clear precedence, schema/types/docs, and focused runner/fallback tests.

options.title: Use existing timeout surfaces
options.body: Document provider timeoutSeconds, run timeout, idle watchdog, and first-event timeout as the supported controls and close or retitle this issue to a docs/config clarification.

options.title: Split by failure mode
options.body: Keep this issue for schema/config design while routing repetition loops and model-specific thinking hangs to narrower canonical issues or PRs.

recommendation.title: Add generation timeout contract
recommendation.body: Add a documented per-agent/per-model non-resetting generation timeout with clear precedence, schema/types/docs, and focused runner/fallback tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already provided the clearest maintainer-facing issue analysis distinguishing adjacent timeout controls from the missing config contract.
